metadata.case_name: WONG SUN CHEONG, SUING BY HIS NEXT FRIEND LEE YIN SHEUNG v. CHOI CHI KONG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: delivery man at Kai Ming Food Shop (Shop B, Ground Floor, 4 Kai Ming Street, To Kwa Wan); also did part-time delivery work (soya milk and noodles)

injuries.description: severe head injuries / traumatic brain injury
source: P sustained severe head injuries as is borne out by the agreed medical evidence.

injuries.description: fractures on the left side of his skull
source: Radiological investigations showed fractures on the left side of his skull, subarachnoid bleeding, subdural bleeding as well as contusion of the brain substance.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures involving skull or facial bones

injuries.description: post-traumatic epilepsy / epileptic seizures (status epilepticus in August 2012)
source: In August 2012, while having lunch at home, he developed status epilepticus with refractory generalized epileptic seizures.
He was then started on the antiepileptic drug phenytoin which he continues to take.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: P was knocked unconscious as a result of the collision.
prolonged post-traumatic amnesia (post‑traumatic amnesia is estimated as over one month)
dysphasia (problem with language); impaired ability to express himself (often using the wrong words) and impaired understanding of verbal communications
cognitive dysfunction; scored 18/30 on mini mental state examination (mild to moderate dementia); naming difficulty; slowed comprehension of terms and instructions
epileptic seizures (status epilepticus in August 2012); started on phenytoin and has been seizure-free since that one occasion
mild spasticity of the right leg with heightened reflexes
truncal ataxia; walked stably but could not walk heel to toe; able to stand with feet together and eyes closed
The craniectomy scar on the left side of his skull was noted.
with P’s cognitive dysfunction, dysphasia, incontinence and impaired balance, P was not employable in any capacity.

treatments_received: Emergency operation to evacuate blood clots and to insert a ventricular drain
Further emergency operation the following day to evacuate more blood clots
Cranioplasty to repair the skull defect with a metallic prosthesis (May 2012)
Admission to intensive care unit and intubation during status epilepticus (August 2012)
Started on the antiepileptic drug phenytoin which he continues to take
Followed up every 3 months by neurosurgeons at QEH

losses.description: P sustained severe head injuries as is borne out by the agreed medical evidence.
cognitive dysfunction; scored 18/30 on mini mental state examination (mild to moderate dementia); naming difficulty; slowed comprehension of terms and instructions
dysphasia (problem with language); impaired ability to express himself (often using the wrong words) and impaired understanding of verbal communications
P is not capable of managing his own legal and financial affairs and is not fully independent even inside the home; needs care and attention for the rest of his life
with P’s cognitive dysfunction, dysphasia, incontinence and impaired balance, P was not employable in any capacity. His permanent loss of earning capacity was 100%.
